# AI Solutions Architect — MRO

**Company:** MRO
**Position:** AI Solutions Architect
**Category:** Information Technology
**Location:** Remote
**Type:** Full-time
**Salary:** $106,000 – $144,000/year + annual cash bonus
**Source:** https://careers-mrocorp.icims.com/jobs/1257/ai-solutions-architect/job
**Date:** 2026-06-25

---

## Role Overview

The AI Solutions Architect is an experienced, hands-on builder, consultant, and enabler — embedded with MRO's business units to deliver white-glove AI enablement, bespoke workflow engineering, solution consulting, and training. The role pairs direct delivery in assigned business areas with curation of the AI capabilities and context layer (prompt libraries, skills, resource libraries, and workflows) that amplify team effectiveness across the organization.

Key characteristics: Product-minded, outcome-oriented, comfortable coordinating with multidisciplinary stakeholders, serves as internal and external thought leader on AI in healthcare, supports principal leadership with AI strategy and planning.

## Core Responsibilities

### Delivery & Enablement
- Deliver white-glove AI enablement, consulting, and solution engineering across assigned business units: tool setup, training, workflow configuration, ongoing support
- Build bespoke AI workflows, agents, and full-stack lightweight internal tools tailored to each area's needs
- Provide solution consulting: assess team workflows, identify AI opportunities, scope and deliver improvements

### Content & Knowledge Curation
- Curate MRO prompt libraries, skill repositories, and agent context in partnership with Principal Architects and Engineers
- Create and maintain playbooks, documentation, and knowledge base for AI tools and workflows

### Training & Coaching
- Design and deliver role-specific AI training and coaching for assigned populations, including focused enablement for senior leaders

### Strategy & Thought Leadership
- Gather and synthesize feedback on AI adoption barriers and report insights to leadership
- Develop customer-facing thought leadership: posts, articles, conference presentations on AI in healthcare
- Support principal leadership on AI strategy, planning, team coordination, and R&D methodology

## Qualifications

### Required
- Demonstrated depth in applied AI: hands-on experience building LLM-based applications, agents, and prompt engineering at scale, including running statistical or structured evaluations of AI outputs
- Proficient with AI and agentic coding tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Github Copilot)
- Strong software-engineering or technical foundation, including proficiency in Python and familiarity with at least one major cloud AI platform (GCP Vertex AI, Azure AI, or AWS Bedrock)
- Experience with Healthcare IT, HIPAA guardrails, and responsible-AI
- Demonstrated initiative and self-direction in AI (self-directed learning, side projects, internal AI experiments); often the recognized go-to person for AI questions
- Excellent communication skills for consulting, training, documentation, and cross-team stakeholder engagement
- Patient, consultative, "let's figure this out together," optimistic team player

### Preferred
- Experience with clinical data workflows, especially FHIR and EHR integrations
- Strong understanding of MRO's business lines, systems, and stakeholder landscape
- Experience with C#/.NET, Ruby on Rails, and/or Python
- Familiarity with containerized microservice architectures and CI/CD pipelines
- Background in technology consulting, enablement, training delivery, or internal center-of-excellence models
- Published technical content or open-source AI contributions

## Benefits
- Annual cash bonus
- Medical, dental, vision, life insurance
- 401(k) plan

---

## Match Assessment

**Rating:** Moderate

**Strengths:**
- CoSH is a production agent runtime — multi-step orchestration, structured JSON evaluation, 43-flag condition engine, prompt engineering at scale
- FlareGuard = bespoke AI workflow engineering deployed to non-technical business teams
- Daily Claude Code/Copilot user — "agentic coding tools" requirement met exactly
- Python + TypeScript — strong technical foundation
- Cross-functional consulting, training, documentation, enablement — all core strengths
- "Go-to person for AI questions" — was exactly this at Redwood
- Self-directed AI projects (CoSH, FlareGuard) demonstrate initiative
- Published technical content via portfolio/case studies

**Gaps:**
- Healthcare IT / HIPAA / responsible AI is a hard requirement — not in profile
- FHIR / EHR / clinical data workflows — new territory
- MRO is healthcare tech (medical records/compliance) — domain gap
- No specific cloud AI platform experience (Vertex AI, Azure AI, Bedrock)

**Notes:**
- No cover letter mentioned
- Resume should emphasize: production AI agent building, prompt engineering at scale, structured evaluation, enablement/training, cross-functional consulting, self-directed projects
- Healthcare domain gap is the main barrier — frame transferable skills (responsible AI, structured validation, compliance-adjacent work like ADA)

materials.cover_letter:
I’ve been building AI workflows and the evaluation systems to prove they work for seven years. Your AI Solutions Architect role caught my attention because it’s exactly what I do: assess teams, build bespoke agents, and document everything so it scales. MRO’s focus on healthcare IT and responsible AI aligns with the kind of systematic, safety-first work I’ve been doing.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation workflow that cut escalations by 70-80%. I designed automated benchmarks and regression detection to catch hallucinations before they hit production. I also redesigned a 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation and automated the documentation pipeline with Playwright screenshots. That mix of hands-on AI engineering and cross-team consulting is what I’d bring to your business units.

I’m ready to deliver white-glove AI enablement, build lightweight internal tools, and curate prompt libraries that actually get used. Let’s talk.
